about: Per-page help for Cosmic Library. Read by assets/js/codex.js (the ? help panel, first-visit hints, the low-graphics switch) and by scripts/build_user_guide.mjs (docs/USER_GUIDE.md). Check with: node scripts/build_user_guide.mjs --check

index.title: Home
index.what: The front door: a tour of every page, tonight's sky over your city and a zoom from a proton to the universe.
try: Pick a mood under "Where do you want to start?" and follow the suggested pages.
Drag the handle under "Drag from a proton to the universe" to feel the powers of ten.
Press "Use my location" to see tonight's sky for where you are (optional; nothing is sent anywhere).

launch.title: Saturn V launch
launch.what: Ride Apollo 11 from the launch pad to Earth orbit, with live telemetry computed from the real flight report.
try: Press Launch (or Space) and watch the director camera follow the climb.
Try the cameras: 1 Director, 2 Pad, 3 Track, 4 Chase, 5 Onboard, 6 Free.
Speed things up with the time-warp buttons or [ and ].
Open Telemetry to see speed, altitude and the rocket equation update live.

data.offline: Everything is built in your browser, so it works offline.

booster.title: Booster landing
booster.what: Land a reusable first stage on a drone ship or back at the launch site, by hand or with the autopilot.
try: Pick a scenario (Drone ship, Return to launch site or Final approach).
Press "Watch the autopilot" first to see a good landing.
Then press "Fly it yourself": W / S throttle, A / D tilt, Space to light the engines, G for legs.
Watch the dashed yellow predicted path: land with it on the pad and your speed near zero.

black-hole.what: A real-time ray tracer that bends light around a black hole, the way Einstein's general relativity says it should.
try: Drag to orbit and watch the disk's light wrap over the top of the hole.

Press "Fall in" to ride toward the event horizon.
Open the Calculator tab to see how time slows near the hole.

data.text: Every pixel is traced through Schwarzschild spacetime in your graphics card. The EHT tab shows the real Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) images.

orbits.title: Orbit Lab
orbits.what: Five hands-on experiments: Newton's cannonball, Kepler's laws, a Hohmann transfer, a gravity assist and Lagrange points.
try: In Cannonball (1), press Fire (Space) at 6.2, then at circular speed, then at escape speed.
In Kepler (2), turn on the equal-area wedges and watch the planet speed up near the Sun.
In Hohmann (3), pick Earth → Mars and see the two burns.
In Lagrange (5), click the canvas to drop test particles.
